intro.title: useOnlineStatus
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component that displays whether the user's device is currently connected to the internet. You will learn how to use the browser's built-in navigator.onLine property to detect online status. The core concept involves creating a reactive service that listens for online/offline events and updates a component's state accordingly. You'll use Angular services, RxJS Observables, and component data binding to make the status update in real-time. By the end, you'll have a functional component that shows 'Online' or 'Offline' based on the network connection.
intro.usecase: The useOnlineStatus pattern is essential for building resilient applications that handle network connectivity changes gracefully. In e-commerce platforms like Amazon, it powers the 'offline mode' indicator that appears when users lose internet access during checkout. Travel booking sites use it to show connection status warnings when users search for flights in areas with spotty Wi-Fi. Developers implement this to disable form submissions, queue offline actions, or display cached content when connectivity drops, ensuring users always know their connection state.
